subject: ventures/str-occupancy-tax-calculator
professional: a state and local tax (SALT) accountant who files lodging and occupancy tax returns for short-term-rental hosts. They would check first (1) what the taxable base includes (cleaning fee, guest/service fees, other charges), (2) the length-of-stay exemption that removes long stays from occupancy tax (Texas 30 consecutive days, Florida over 182 nights, Tennessee 89 nights / local first-30-days), and (3) which layers the platform actually collects for the listing's address, before trusting any per-layer split

evidence.correctness: Ran calc.mjs on 10 probes (node /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/6c791d2a-28ff-5e31-aaa5-e982a8d2dec3/scratchpad/str-occ/probe/probes.mjs). Rates and collection status were taken from sources the author did not write: Airbnb Help Center articles 2301 (Florida), 2331 (Texas), 2330 (Tennessee), fetched 2026-11-15; Texas Comptroller hotel-tax page and FAQ (6 percent; houses rented 30+ consecutive days not taxed); Florida DOR discretionary sales surtax page (surtax applies to transient rentals). Passes: (P2) Lee County FL stay, $180 x 3 + $95 cleaning, 6% state + 0.5% surtax + 5% TDT all collected by Airbnb per article 2301: hand 635 base, 38.10 + 3.18 + 31.75 = 73.03, host 0; tool identical. (P7) mixed rates 6.35%/2.75% on 533.28 plus $2/night flat fee half collected: hand 33.86 + 14.67 + 10 = 58.53, host 19.67; tool identical. (P1) worked example 1150 x 6% = 69, x 5% = 57.50: identical. Fails: (P3) a 30-night Texas stay is taxed $487.50 with $262.50 shown as the host's own filing; the Comptroller exempts stays of 30+ consecutive days and Airbnb collects only on reservations of 29 nights and shorter, so the correct figure is $0, and no warning appears. (P5) Tennessee local occupancy tax applies to the first 30 days only (article 2330); a 45-night $100 stay at 5% should be $150, tool $225. (P4) Tennessee taxes the listing price including guest fees; there is no guest-fee input, so a $570 charge is taxed on $500 ($35.00 vs $39.90). The arithmetic is exact; the outputs are wrong whenever stay length or base composition matters, with no warning. Score 2.
evidence.completeness: Claimed features checked against the code and by running: up to four named layers with per-layer platform share (works, P1/P2/P7); flat per-night fee with its own platform share (works, P7); monthly rollup (works, calc.test.mjs:26-28); split / host-remits-all / platform-remits-all / zero-rate warnings (work); share link and browser save (share.test.mjs passes); local opt-out usage counter (usage.test.mjs passes); three article pages present and linked; served page and llms.txt load at marisstella.app (200). One claimed feature does not exist: the comparison page says the calculator flags 'a layer entered at a rate but never marked as either fully covered or fully uncovered ... on every stay' (vs-tracking-it-in-a-spreadsheet.html:79), but a blank platform share silently reads as 0% (calc.mjs:73) and only the ordinary split warning fires (P6). README test count is stale (46 stated, 53 run). Score 3.
evidence.verification: `cd ventures/str-occupancy-tax-calculator && node --test '*.test.mjs'`: 53 tests, 53 pass, 0.15 s. Five mutants with platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: 3 caught (cleaning fee dropped from base :153, round2 epsilon removed :37, host share = full amount :99), 2 survived (flat-fee platform share forced to 0 :157, lower-bound check loosened to min-1 :80). The only flat-fee test uses a 0% platform share (calc.test.mjs:53), so a bug that ignored the platform's share of the flat fee would ship. All tests are the author's own example; none uses a long stay or a published jurisdiction's rates. Score 2.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (219 lines), index.html (486), share.mjs, usage.mjs and the test files. Pure, dependency-free, half-away-from-zero rounding documented and correct, bounds-checked inputs, labelled per-row errors, output written with textContent. Defects: readNumber uses Number.parseFloat (calc.mjs:74), so '1,200' is read as 1 and '12abc' as 12 without an error (P8; the page's type=number inputs mostly shield this, the engine and share decode do not); fractional nights accepted (P9); blank platform share is indistinguishable from an explicit 0%. Score 3.
evidence.claims: Backed: no-warranty and 'makes no determination' disclaimers on every page (page.test.mjs:113); no network requests (grep and page.test.mjs:123); worked-example figures on README, index and both articles match calc.mjs (page.test.mjs:92-108, :169); 'most jurisdictions tax the cleaning fee' (Airbnb FL/TX/TN articles all say 'including any cleaning fee'); the FL pattern of state collected and county TDT not is real for counties absent from Airbnb article 2301 (e.g. Walton, Okaloosa, Monroe, Duval). Unbacked: the 'raises that flag on every stay' feature (vs-tracking-it-in-a-spreadsheet.html:79 and its JSON-LD, P6); 'A platform's payout summary and 1099-K report what it paid you and what it remitted on your behalf' (how-much-occupancy-tax-will-i-have-to-self-file-this-year.html:36): IRS 1099-K instructions, Box 1a, report gross payment transactions, with no remitted-tax box; the default row labelled 'Florida state sales tax' at 6% omits the 0.5-1.5% discretionary surtax that Florida DOR applies to transient rentals; README '46 assertions' (README.md:20) vs 53 tests. Score 2.
evidence.fitness: Job: a host with a listing in an uncovered county wants to know what to set aside and file each period. For an ordinary stay under 30 nights the tool gives the right per-layer split once the host has found the rates and the platform's coverage themselves (the hard part; the how-to article points to the right places). It cannot take the filing period's actual bookings (only one representative stay times bookings per month), has no guest/other-fee base, and on monthly or mid-term stays it reports a tax the host does not owe. A SALT accountant would use it as a scratch split for short stays, not as a return worksheet. Score 2.
evidence.domain: Compared with the Texas Comptroller (HOT 6%, stays of 30+ consecutive days not taxed), Florida DOR (surtax on transient rentals) and Airbnb's per-state collection articles (FL 182-night, TX 29-night, TN 89-night thresholds; TN base includes guest fees; TN local occupancy on first 30 days only). The per-authority collection model and inclusion of the cleaning fee match practice. Departures: no length-of-stay exemption or day cap of any kind (nights accepted to 365, calc.mjs:55); taxable base fixed to nightly x nights + cleaning (calc.mjs:153) with no guest-fee or other-fee line; flat fee modelled per night only (not per room-night or per stay); per-stay layer rounding rather than the return-level computation a filing uses. Score 2.

verdict: A small, clean, honest-in-tone per-layer occupancy-tax splitter whose arithmetic is exact: three stays recomputed from Airbnb's own Florida rates and by hand (73.03, 58.53, 126.50) match to the cent. It misses what a SALT accountant checks first. There is no length-of-stay rule: a 30-night Texas stay shows $262.50 to self-file where the Comptroller says no tax is due, and Tennessee's first-30-days local cap is ignored ($225 vs $150). The base cannot include guest fees, which Tennessee taxes. The comparison page claims an 'unmarked layer' flag that does not exist, and an article misdescribes the 1099-K. 53/53 tests pass; 2 of 5 seeded mutants survive, including the flat fee's platform share. Scores: correctness 2, completeness 3, verification 2, craft 3, claims 2, fitness 2, domain 2. Finished by its own feature list, not at the bar.
